name: example-app
concept: Penny Jar, a personal expense tracker in Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, minSdk 26. Users sign in with email and password, log expenses with receipt photos and sync them to the Penny Jar backend over a REST API. Features: biometric app unlock, private notes on expenses encrypted on the device, share links for monthly reports, automatic backup, help pages in a WebView opened from the app and from deep links, place tagging for expenses, Mixpanel analytics with a consent screen, a support form and settings. Two Gradle modules: :app (UI and features) and :sync (a library module: REST client, receipt upload, receipts database and a content provider).
notes: IDs checked against the tagged releases above on 2026-11-21. Only IDs are cited; no OWASP text is copied.

MASWE v1.0.0 renumbered the weakness IDs, but MASTG v2.0.0 tests still point to the old beta IDs (MASTG-TEST-0231 names beta MASWE-0001, which is MASWE-0005 in v1.0.0). This key uses MASWE v1.0.0 IDs. Each MASWE v1.0.0 file lists its beta IDs under mappings.maswe-beta.
MASTG test IDs are from tests-beta/android (the v2 tests). The older tests/android are all deprecated in v2.0.0.

One OWASP mapping disagrees: MASTG-TEST-0334 tests JavaScript bridges (addJavascriptInterface) but names beta MASWE-0069, which v1.0.0 maps to MASWE-0034. EA-15 uses MASWE-0033, the v1.0.0 weakness for JavaScript bridges.
A location is a file path relative to the app root plus an anchor: text that occurs exactly once in that file. Step 02 makes every anchor exist; the scorer turns anchors into lines.
No issue needs a running app, so none is NEEDS DYNAMIC.

items.title: Password saved in plain text for 'remember me'
items.planted: When 'remember me' is ticked, the login flow stores the user's email and password as plain strings in SharedPreferences.
items.fix: Don't store the password. Keep only the session token, encrypted with an AES key held in the Android Keystore.

items.title: Automatic backup writes all transactions to shared storage
items.planted: A periodic WorkManager job writes every expense (date, amount, merchant, note) to a CSV file in the public Documents folder, using WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and requestLegacyExternalStorage. With minSdk 26, on Android 8 to 10 any app with storage permission can read it. On every version the file outlives an uninstall and is readable in the Files app, over USB and by apps with all-files access.
items.fix: Write the automatic backup to app-private storage. Export to shared storage only when the user asks, through the system file picker (ACTION_CREATE_DOCUMENT). Remove the storage permission.

items.title: HTTP bodies and auth headers logged in release builds
items.planted: The REST client in :sync always adds an OkHttp logging interceptor at body level. Another interceptor adds the Authorization header, so tokens, emails and expense data reach logcat in release builds.
items.fix: Add the logging interceptor only in debug builds, at basic level, and redact the Authorization header.

items.title: Backups include stored credentials
items.planted: allowBackup is true and there are no backup or data extraction rules, so the SharedPreferences file with the saved password (EA-01) goes into cloud backups and device transfers.
items.fix: Add data extraction rules (and full backup content for older versions) that exclude the credentials and token files.

items.title: Helpdesk API token with write access hardcoded in the app
items.planted: The support form posts tickets straight to a third-party helpdesk API with an account-wide API token stored as a constant. Anyone who unpacks the APK can read, edit or delete every ticket.
items.fix: Remove the token from the app. Send support requests to the Penny Jar backend, which holds the token.

items.title: Hardcoded AES key for private notes
items.planted: Private notes are encrypted with an AES key built from a constant byte array in one file and used by the cipher in another. The key is the same on every install.
items.fix: Generate the AES key in the Android Keystore on first use and never export it.

items.title: Private notes encrypted with AES in ECB mode
items.planted: The note cipher uses AES/ECB/PKCS5Padding, so equal plaintext blocks give equal ciphertext blocks.
items.fix: Use AES/GCM/NoPadding with a fresh random IV per note, stored next to the ciphertext.

items.title: Share-link tokens from a non-cryptographic random generator
items.planted: Share links for monthly reports use a token made with java.util.Random: a non-cryptographic generator with 48 bits of state (CWE-338). The tokens are far easier to guess than a 128-bit secure token, and one generator's output predicts its later tokens.
items.fix: Make the token with SecureRandom (at least 128 bits), or let the backend issue it.

items.title: Biometric unlock not bound to a key
items.planted: App unlock calls BiometricPrompt without a CryptoObject and sets an 'unlocked' flag in the success callback. Hooking the callback bypasses the lock.
items.fix: Authenticate with a CryptoObject for a Keystore key that requires user authentication, and decrypt the session token with it only on success.

items.title: Cleartext traffic allowed, receipt images over HTTP
items.planted: The release network security config permits cleartext in its base config, and receipt images load from an http:// base URL.
items.fix: Set cleartextTrafficPermitted to false in the base config and use https:// for the image host.

items.title: Receipt upload trusts any certificate and any host
items.planted: The upload client uses an X509TrustManager whose checks are empty and a hostname verifier that always returns true.
items.fix: Delete the custom trust manager and hostname verifier and use the platform defaults.

items.title: Receipts content provider exported without a permission
items.planted: The :sync library's own manifest declares the receipts content provider with exported="true" and no permission. The app's manifest doesn't mention it; it only appears in the merged manifest. Any installed app can read every receipt.
items.fix: Set exported="false" on the provider; nothing outside the app uses it.

items.title: SQL injection through the receipts provider
items.planted: The provider passes a URI path segment (a merchant name) to a query helper in another file, which concatenates it into raw SQL.
items.fix: Use a parameterised query with selection arguments.

items.title: Deep link opens any URL in the help WebView
items.planted: A pennyjar:// deep link declared in the manifest opens the help activity, which loads the 'page' query parameter into its JavaScript-enabled WebView without checking the host.
items.fix: Load only https URLs on the help host (allow-list), and open anything else in the browser.

items.title: WebView JavaScript bridge hands out the session token
items.planted: The help WebView adds a JavaScript interface whose methods include one that returns the current session token. With EA-14, any web page can steal it.
items.fix: Remove the token method from the bridge; the help pages don't need it.

items.title: WebView remote debugging always on
items.planted: Application.onCreate enables WebView contents debugging unconditionally, in release builds too.
items.fix: Enable it only in debug builds, or remove it.

items.title: Release build is debuggable
items.planted: The release build type sets isDebuggable = true. Play Console rejects debuggable uploads, and a debuggable app can be attached to and inspected.
items.fix: Remove isDebuggable from the release build type.

items.title: targetSdk below Play's requirement
items.planted: targetSdk is 34. Since 31 August 2026, Play accepts new apps and updates only if they target API 36 or higher.
items.fix: Target API 36.

items.title: Gson version with a known vulnerability
items.planted: The version catalog pins Gson 2.8.5, affected by CVE-2022-25647 (fixed in 2.8.9).
items.fix: Upgrade Gson to a current release.

items.title: Analytics starts before the user consents
items.planted: Mixpanel is initialised and tracks app-open events in Application.onCreate. The consent screen, shown later, only stores the user's answer; nothing checks it before tracking.
items.fix: Initialise Mixpanel opted out by default and opt in only after the user consents; opt out again if they decline.

items.title: Email used as the analytics user ID
items.planted: After login, analytics identifies the user by email address and sends the merchant name with every expense event.
items.fix: Identify users by a random internal ID from the backend, and don't send merchant names.

items.title: Precise and background location for city tagging
items.planted: To tag an expense with a city, the app requests fine and background location. Coarse foreground location is enough, and Play reviews background location requests strictly.
items.fix: Request only ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION, in the foreground, when the user taps 'tag place'. Remove background location.

items.title: No way to delete the account in the app
items.planted: Users can create an account, but settings offer only sign-out. Play requires apps that allow account creation to let users delete the account from within the app.
items.fix: Add 'Delete account' to settings: call the backend's delete endpoint, clear local data and sign out.

items.title: MD5 used for thumbnail cache file names
items.whyFine: MD5 only turns a receipt image URL into a cache file name. No security property depends on it.

items.title: Non-secure random for avatar colours
items.whyFine: Random picks a placeholder avatar colour. Predicting it harms nothing.

items.title: Cleartext to the emulator host in debug builds
items.whyFine: The debug source set's network config allows cleartext only to 10.0.2.2 (the emulator's host, for a local mock server). It isn't part of release builds.

items.title: Exported launcher activity
items.whyFine: The launcher activity must be exported so the home screen can start it, and it reads no input from the intent.

items.title: Mixpanel project token in the code
items.whyFine: Mixpanel's project token is public by design: it only says which project events go to and grants no access.

items.title: FileProvider for sharing receipt images
items.whyFine: The FileProvider isn't exported, grants temporary read access per URI, and its paths cover only the shared-images cache folder.
